import tkinter as tk
from tkinter import filedialog
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

class DataTrendAnalyzer:
    def __init__(self):
        self.root = tk.Tk()
        self.root.title("Data Trend Analyzer")

        self.frame = tk.Frame(self.root)
        self.frame.pack()

        # Create a button to import data

        self.import_button.pack()

        # Create a button to analyze data
        self.analyze_button = tk.Button(self.frame, text="Analyze Data", command=self.analyze_data)
        self.analyze_button.pack()

        # Create a label to display the analysis results
        self.result_label = tk.Label(self.frame, text="")
        self.result_label.pack()

    def import_data(self):
        # Open a file dialog to select the data file
        file_path = filedialog.askopenfilename()

        # Read the data file into a pandas DataFrame
        self.data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

        # Display the data in the user interface
        self.result_label['text'] = "Data imported successfully"

    def analyze_data(self):
        # Perform linear regression on the data
        X = self.data['Time']
        y = self.data['Value']
        model = LinearRegression()
        model.fit(X.values.reshape(-1, 1), y)

        # Display the analysis results in the user interface
        self.result_label['text'] = "Linear regression coefficients: {:.2f}, {:.2f}".format(model.coef_[0], model.intercept_)

    def run(self):
        self.root.mainloop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    analyzer = DataTrendAnalyzer()
    analyzer.run()
```

This example provides a basic user interface for importing data and analyzing it using linear regression. However, it is just a starting point, and the software would need to be expanded to include more features and analysis options.
